summary: Discernment: wisdom as a cultivated ability to see clearly. In Buddhist use 慧 often renders prajñā, while 智 can carry jñāna in other contexts.

satellites.title: The Faculty of Wisdom
satellites.evidence: The five faculties culminate in 慧根. A list places it next to concentration, but does not say the two practices are equivalent.

satellites.title: Why 般若 Was Kept by Sound
satellites.evidence: Xuanzang named five kinds of word to transcribe rather than translate. The fifth is 生善故, “to give rise to the good”: 般若尊重，智慧輕淺 — prajñā is weighty, 智慧 is slight. So 慧 can render prajñā in a list, while the sūtras keep 般若 by its sound.
satellites.caveat: Xuanzang’s rule is reported five centuries later, in the prefatory matter of the Fanyi mingyi ji (1143).
